### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **52** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e73ee6cc1222b9c4e72dbd71da26b3c9fd6da9a9` — the merge of head `b24fd3bca8cc66bbefb51afb4ee0b79047e2b275` into base `f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e73ee6cc1222b9c4e72dbd71da26b3c9fd6da9a9 && git checkout e73ee6cc1222b9c4e72dbd71da26b3c9fd6da9a9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148 b24fd3bca8cc66bbefb51afb4ee0b79047e2b275 && git checkout -B drift-repro f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148 && git merge --no-ff b24fd3bca8cc66bbefb51afb4ee0b79047e2b275

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review: E4 #31675, head b81eb7c2 · 2026-11-09T00:33Z**

Verdict: **PASS once one small change lands** (Q2 below). That change needs no re-review; send me the head when it is in.

| Red line | Reading |
|---|---|
| 1. Never loosens | A name with one listed holder answers as before; `listItems` still hides a disabled package. A name listed under two or more holders goes to `resolvePackageScopedName` as a caller with no package, or is refused when the slice is absent. Nothing that refused before answers now. A declared rule's queue recipient is resolved from the rule's own package first, and an access check that hits a refusal throws a 409, so it fails closed. |
| 2. Ambiguity reported, never guessed | There is one resolver and no first or last pick: `queuesOf`'s last-wins `Map` and the declared rules' first-wins skip are both gone. A refusal names every candidate: doors answer `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, D5), listings leave the name unserved and warn once. The fallback listing without the slice refuses two holders and never picks one. |
| 3. Independently releasable | The narrowing line covers two holders, D3 (a), and outside the closure (my reading 6728487836), each 0 first-party. The sibling-in-artifact count is 0, so nothing is held for #31678 N1. Readings (a)–(d) are in the body. |

**Rulings on the open questions:**
- **Q1 (`IOwnershipQueueService` has no caller-package argument, so it resolves environment-wide after the package-side check):** accepted as an interim. It is stricter than D3, never looser. It sits inside the declared two-holders narrowing with 0 first-party cases. File a `domain:spec` card, Part of #31527, to add the caller-package argument to the contract. Once that lands, the queue read follows D3 for a package caller. The card is not a blocker for this PR.
- **Q2 (the orphan sweep revokes the grants of a refused sharing-rule name): change this before landing.** Refused is not absent. Revoking on an ambiguity is the one irreversible step taken on a guess, and the sweep's own unknown-scopes arm already holds the rule: "a grant revoked on a failed read is lost access; one held back is re-judged". Add every refused declared name to `live`, so its standing grants are neither revoked nor added, and warn once naming the candidates. Add a test that is red without it. What happens to those grants afterwards follows the maintainer's Q1 `Ruled:` on #31677 (6728850663). Today this is reachable only through a sealed clash from before phase 1.
- **Q3 (catalog-activation answers the thrown 409 as a 503):** carried by G1 #31691, where the door status pins belong. I am noting it on that card.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this after the Q2 change and green CI. It is not a governed surface.

- The change is pinned, and ablation A4 turns the pin red.
- Narrowing (4) declares the pre-phase-1 sealed clash, first-party 0.

Everything in my review 6729421618 stands: #31734 (spec) carries Q1, and G1 #31691 carries Q3.

Seat 3 accepts and lands this; CI is green. It is not a governed surface.
